Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork using standard intake forms, versioned registers, and dated sign-off fields; each document carries a unique identifier, a preparer reference, and a review date, with access tracked through named account records and change logs.
2) What occurred: The actor prepared a dated planning document describing a staged disruption of clinical system availability, leaving the risk-assessment sign-off field unverified. The actor drafted a technical specification naming encryption and recovery-disable procedures, with the security-approval field left unverified. The actor compiled a list of target systems referencing host identifiers, leaving the change-control authorization field unverified. The actor prepared a communication outline for senior administration, with the legal-review sign-off left unverified. The actor outlined trace-avoidance steps, leaving the compliance certification field unverified. The actor stored the materials in a shared folder under a personal account name, with the access-grant justification field left unverified.
3) Materials/access observed: A planning document with a preparation date field; a technical specification referencing system components; a host inventory list with identifier fields; a communication outline with recipient title fields; an access list naming a personal account with elevated privileges; a shared folder location reference; and a change-log entry dated within the review period.
4) Indicators & artifacts: The unverified risk-assessment sign-off field in the planning document; the unverified security-approval field in the technical specification; the unverified change-control authorization field in the host inventory; the unverified legal-review sign-off in the communication outline; the unverified compliance certification field in the trace-avoidance notes; and the unverified access-grant justification field in the account records.
